metadata.title: Cloud Platform-as-a-Service Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for securely consuming provider-managed application platforms where the operating system and runtime are not directly controlled by the consumer.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Cloud platform services including managed runtimes, function platforms, application services, and provider-managed execution environments.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Pattern for establishing trust assumptions and shared responsibility boundaries for Platform-as-a-Service environments.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: PaaS trust assumptions depend on the underlying hosting model and provider operational controls.

props.name: depends-on
props.remarks: PaaS security relies on trusted cloud management and automation control planes.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Initial access via misconfigured application services or exposed PaaS endpoints.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Privilege escalation through misconfigured service identities or excessive PaaS permissions.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Defense evasion by modifying PaaS configuration, logging, or monitoring settings.

props.name: attack-tactic
props.remarks: Collection of sensitive data from provider-managed application platforms.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Exploitation of exposed application services or platform endpoints.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Abuse of valid identities associated with PaaS services or service principals.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Privileged access management for PaaS service identities and administrators.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Configuration hardening and validation for provider-managed platform services.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Monitoring and auditing of application platform behavior and configuration changes.

metadata.remarks: Cloud Platform-as-a-Service Core defines the foundational trust properties required to safely consume provider-managed application platforms. This pattern explicitly recognizes that the runtime and operating system are outside consumer control, shifting trust to configuration, identity, data access, and provider-managed security controls.

components.title: PaaS Runtime Trust Boundary
components.description: Defines trust boundaries between consumer workloads and provider-managed runtimes.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Consumers rely on provider controls for runtime isolation and security enforcement.

components.title: PaaS Configuration Responsibility
components.description: Ensures consumer-managed configuration within PaaS environments is explicitly governed.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Configuration settings owned by the consumer are explicitly understood and managed.

components.title: PaaS Service Identity Control
components.description: Controls identities and permissions used by PaaS services and applications.

implemented-requirements.remarks: PaaS service identities are constrained to minimum required privileges.
